title: RBI holds repo rate at 6.50%, raises FY25 growth forecast to 7.2%
summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee unanimously held the repo rate at 6.50% and kept its withdrawal-of-accommodation stance for a sixth consecutive meeting. Governor Shaktikanta Das said inflation was on a glide path to 4% but warned of risks from an uncertain monsoon. The MPC raised its FY25 GDP growth forecast to 7.2% from 7.0%, citing strong rural demand recovery.

sentiment.rationale: Straight policy reporting with no evaluative framing. Slight tilt comes from the upward growth-forecast revision being a positive signal.

key_claims.claim: The MPC voted unanimously to hold the repo rate at 6.50%.
The withdrawal-of-accommodation stance was retained for the sixth consecutive meeting.
Retail inflation eased to 4.83% in April.
Food price volatility from an uncertain monsoon could disrupt the inflation trajectory.
The MPC raised the FY25 GDP growth forecast to 7.2% from 7.0%.

aspects.evidence: MPC held the repo rate at 6.50% for a sixth consecutive meeting.
Inflation eased to 4.83% in April and is described as on a glide path to the 4% target.
FY25 growth forecast raised to 7.2% from 7.0% citing strong rural demand.
Governor warned an uncertain monsoon could disrupt the inflation trajectory through food prices.
Pickup in private capex cited as a contributor to the upward growth revision.

quotes.text: On a glide path to the 4% medium-term target.
quotes.speaker: Shaktikanta Das
